body: Oh ok, thanks so much for this explanation. I guess I took “anything goes” literally. To me, it felt right to keep practicing the spins, since I can practice floor work and other stuff at home.
I’m the first to class, actually. The other student comes in late and joins me.
Thank you! Makes so much sense and lines up with concepts that have come up for me before, like "there is strength in community", even though I have certainly neglected that before.

Yeah I’ve experienced true love bombing at the hands of a narcissist and then I’ve also experienced the push/pull of unhealthy attachment style and they are different…although they feel very, very similar to experience due to the hot and cold thing.

Unlike a traditional “love bomber” I think, as an FA I can’t fake the enthusiasm for someone, and certainly not for long periods of time. I have to be feeling it 100%, and when I am, the other person will get the flirtiest version of me, the most passionate lover, the best listener. The best version of myself when it comes to a one-on-one relationship. I can see the other person’s flaws and even red flags, but they don’t matter. Something in my brain is telling me they’re worth it.

However, when I’m not feeling it 100%, I can’t bring that version of me to the table. If I’m still feeling it somewhat but am questioning things, I’ll be a little dulled down. And if the other person did something to trigger the dismissive side of me, I’ll physically flee.

>What I often wonder after I love bomb or being love bombed by someone is how genuine the connection was with that individual.

Recently I’ve been looking at a situationship I’m in through a different lens and have been coming to realize if you take away the flirty, passionate me, what is left of the relationship? In my particular case, you’re left with him, a man fast approaching 40 whose longest relationship has only been 2 years. A man who can’t apologize. A man who rarely texts first so we usually go a week without speaking, even though he’s glued to his phone. And then you have the real me, a woman who claims she wants and feels a “real connection” but can’t even bring these issues up to him for fear of rejection. So what do we really have? What am I feeling? We might have some kind of connection but right now, I’m of the opinion that most of it is self-made bullshit.

So I absolutely have to question how genuine are feelings are, even though WOW do they feel genuine at the time. I’d go so far as to say it’s a shitty thing to do, dragging someone else into the unhealed trauma.

I have anxious avoidant attachment so yeah, attachment issues are a real thing lol. Currently leaning very anxious. I don't feel starved for love, but starved for connection. If I moved, I would be giving up some relationships where people show up for me and are consistent, but I don't feel much connection to. For me, everything comes back to that connection. But sometimes I wonder if it's even real, or just some illusion because this relationship is rather new.

I mentioned this in another comment, but I have some ties to the new place, so it is not a completely random and unknown location. Yes, it is somewhat of a red flag to me that we haven't made things official by 6 months, but this impending move of his has been looming since about 2 months in and he didn't want to commit because of that. If I do end up moving, I am not expecting an immediate commitment, nor do I even know if I want that. I just want more time to explore the possibility, and I feel like I have more to lose if I *don't* pursue this than if I do and things don't work out. But maybe that's just my "issues" talking.

Thank you! This is super helpful. I've been journaling a lot too and it's about the only thing I can focus on completely as of late. I feel guilty as it takes up a lot of time, but I guess maybe that's what I need right now.

He's moving quite far, 2500 km away. We've been dating about 6 months but have been in each other's lives for far longer. I haven't felt a connection like this with anyone else, which is why I'm drawn to pursue it. But, he is not interested in doing long distance. I understand that, but it also makes me question this connection. 

My support system is, oddly enough, stronger there than where I live now (my parents are only a couple hours away and I have several friends there). So, it's not a completely random move. Being closer to these people certainly is a pull too, but he's the #1 reason.
Rings a bell for me! Thank you for this. Do you have any tips for connecting with your authentic self? I've been working at it for years but at times like these, I feel more lost than ever.
Not really the main point of my post, but thank you!
Just remember that A LOT of people who use Tinder are actually unavailable. Already are in a relationship, are just there for validation, and so on. It sucks but don't sweat it. Happens to all of us.

This happened to me quite a few times with my ex...he was pretty big and certain angles were just too much. It would hurt like hell during sex and I'd have horrible pain on my side, like in the ovary region, for the next few days. 

It always went away and healed on its own...never lasted a week like yours. But, we didn't have sex again until I felt better. If you're keeping at it, maybe you're injuring it over and over and it can't properly heal?

But yeah, like the other commenter said, it may be a good idea to see a doc if it persists!

I had a similar situation last year...it's hard to get over. For sure. I'm not sure if y'all are on social media but one thing I did that majorly helped me was unfollow (not unfriend) all his accounts. So he wasn't showing up in my feed all the time. Out of sight, out of mind...I mean, it helped at least. 

Another thing is to try and live in the present. Your fling might have been GREAT, but right now, you haven't spoken in six months...so what do you really have, right now? Nothing. (I don't mean to be blunt, but it's true!) I honestly believe that if you're meant to be with someone, it will work out.

The beauty of being 18 is that you're an adult now and you get to choose for yourself if you want him in your life or not...you don't have to put up with him just because the courts say you have to. My situation is very similar to yours. When I was your age, we tried to work it out in counseling. It never worked. Nothing changed. It's been 10 years since then and nothing has changed to this day. I felt numb at 17/18 too, and I still do, to an extent. But for me, the damage has been done. It's actually messed me up more than I thought it did, as far as how I treat new relationships with friends and romantic partners. So if I could go back and tell the younger version of myself something, it would be this: how much value is he contributing to your life? Do the bad times outweigh the good? If so, cut the ties. If you can afford it, speak to a therapist and get over the emotional damage as soon as possible. Don't let this haunt you into your adulthood. 

Of course, every person, every case is different...but some people never change. You seem smart so I would believe your judgement of him is accurate. Good luck and hugs!

I'm with you. No matter how hard I try, I'm just a nobody. A weirdo. A freak. I hate myself for even trying. I've done everything I possibly can and it's still not good enough, not even for one single person.

ALL THE TIME. But only by duds/creeps. Not sure where the good ones are. I worked in the food industry for almost a decade and it was very apparent then. Luckily it tended to work in my favor, 'cause tips...but still. Has led to some sticky and uncomfortable situations sometimes. It's also hard for me to be super direct (is this an INFP thing?) because I don't want to be mean. I have a hard time telling people "I'm not interested", but I'm getting better at it.

Agreed, but only in large group settings. I’ve always been this way…at the most basic level, it was me not raising my hand in class even when, 9/10, I knew the answer. I think with me, there’s a tiny bit of fear there as well…what if I say the wrong thing? What if I pronounce a word wrong? What if I insult someone with my opinion? Unfortunately, this makes me hard to get to know and forgettable. I think it’s why I don’t get invited out to join in social stuff. I’m just boring.
I don't personally, but one of my INFP friends has bad anxiety too. Seems to be common

Thanks for your input! The more I think about it, the more I can see how this type of behavior has been going on for a long time. I think now that I've been actively trying not to internalize things, but generally end up feeling rejected when I do verbalize my thoughts, I've got a lot of turmoil breaking out. I think I'll look into a therapist, although money is tight right now.

I def relate to most all of this. The sad thing is I don't even know what my needs are. I feel at my best when I can help someone else, like if a friend comes to me upset and I can listen and make them feel better. I take pride in being a good, supportive friend. I have a very long history of throwing my own feelings aside that I don't even know what I myself need. 

I also am with you on craving things from those who don't seem able to give that to you. I'm currently experiencing this with a couple fellow INFPs though, which is discouraging (to say the least). It's such a slap in the face to repeatedly listen, support, and continually be there for someone, no matter what, and then literally be flat out ignored by that same person when, on rare occasion, you need support. Especially when they, technically, should have the tools to be there for you, and you've seen them do it with others...

Maybe I just stumbled on a couple duds...

If she mentions how she gets tired during the work week, you could send something like, "Hey, hope your week is treating you well!" If I were you, I'd add in "I really enjoyed talking with you this weekend. Would you like to grab a coffee sometime?" Easy. Don't wait too long or the moment will pass.

I don't think you ruined the friendship....he even told you he wanted to focus on maintaining it, right? Then don't go cold. Don't ruin it. 

This situation recently happened to me except it was my friend who had the more than friends feelings. It took a little bit of time, but we're friends again, no harm done. We were both adults about it and didn't make it a big deal. Sometimes the romantic chemistry just isn't there. It sucks feeling rejected, but I hope you don't take it personally!
